meta.titre: Angles and Polygons: Interior and Exterior Angles
meta.sous_theme: Angle facts, parallel lines and regular polygons

sections.contenu_markdown: A tiler in Douala is laying hexagonal paving stones around a fountain. For the stones to fit without gaps, every corner must have exactly the right size, and he does not measure it: he calculates it. The same angle facts decide how roof beams meet, how a football pitch is marked and how a map is drawn. At the GCE you are asked for angles on a line, in triangles, between parallel lines and in regular polygons almost every year, and most of these questions need just one fact applied carefully.

items: A straight line is an angle of $180^\circ$, a right angle is $90^\circ$ and a full turn is $360^\circ$.
A triangle has 3 sides, a quadrilateral 4, a pentagon 5, a hexagon 6, an octagon 8 and a decagon 10.
A regular polygon has all its sides equal and all its angles equal.

sections.contenu_markdown:
**Basic angle facts**

- Angles on a straight line add up to $180^\circ$.
- Angles around a point add up to $360^\circ$.
- Vertically opposite angles are equal.
- The angles of a triangle add up to $180^\circ$; the angles of a quadrilateral add up to $360^\circ$.
- In an isosceles triangle the two angles opposite the equal sides are equal.
- An **exterior angle** of a triangle (a side extended) equals the sum of the two interior opposite angles.

**Polygons with $n$ sides**

| Quantity | Formula |
|---|---|
| Sum of interior angles | $(n-2)\times 180^\circ$ |
| Sum of exterior angles (one at each vertex) | $360^\circ$ |
| Each exterior angle of a regular polygon | $\dfrac{360^\circ}{n}$ |
| Each interior angle of a regular polygon | $180^\circ-\text{exterior angle}$ |

At every vertex the interior angle and the exterior angle lie on a straight line, so they add up to $180^\circ$.

**Reading a diagram.** Write each angle you find on the diagram with a reason, for example "$110^\circ$ (angles on a straight line)". Do not assume that two lines are parallel or two sides are equal unless the question says so.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a line crosses two parallel lines and you need an unknown angle.
variantes.contenu_markdown:
- **Corresponding angles** (F-shape) are equal.
- **Alternate angles** (Z-shape) are equal.
- **Co-interior angles** (C-shape) add up to $180^\circ$.

Example: if a transversal makes an angle of $65^\circ$ with the first parallel line, the alternate angle at the second line is $65^\circ$, and the co-interior angle is $180^\circ-65^\circ=115^\circ$.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question gives one exterior or interior angle of a regular polygon.
variantes.contenu_markdown:
Find the exterior angle first (it is $180^\circ$ minus the interior angle), then use

$$n=\frac{360^\circ}{\text{exterior angle}}$$

The answer must be a whole number; if it is not, you have made an error. For example an exterior angle of $45^\circ$ gives $n=8$, a regular octagon whose interior angles are $135^\circ$ each.

sections.enonce_markdown: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is $156^\circ$. Find (a) the number of sides of the polygon and (b) the sum of its interior angles.

etapes.justification: The interior and exterior angles at a vertex lie on a straight line, so they add up to $180^{\circ}$.
The exterior angles of any polygon add up to $360^{\circ}$ and all of them are equal here.

etapes.action: Find the sum of the interior angles.

etapes.justification: Fifteen equal interior angles of $156^\circ$ must give the same total.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The polygon has $15$ sides and the interior angles add up to $2340^\circ$.

items.erreur_markdown: The sum of the interior angles of a hexagon is $6\times 180^\circ=1080^\circ$.
items.pourquoi_faux: The formula is $(n-2)\times 180^\circ$. Multiplying $n$ by $180^\circ$ forgets that the polygon splits into $n-2$ triangles.

items.erreur_markdown: Co-interior angles between parallel lines are equal.
items.pourquoi_faux: Alternate and corresponding angles are equal, but co-interior angles are supplementary: they add up to $180^\circ$.
items.correction_markdown: If one co-interior angle is $70^\circ$, the other is $180^\circ-70^\circ=110^\circ$.

items.erreur_markdown: Each exterior angle of a regular decagon is $\dfrac{180^\circ}{10}=18^\circ$.
items.pourquoi_faux: The exterior angles add up to $360^\circ$, not $180^\circ$.

items.erreur_markdown: In an isosceles triangle with a $40^\circ$ angle at the top, each base angle is $40^\circ$.
items.pourquoi_faux: The equal angles are the two base angles, and the three angles must add up to $180^\circ$.

items.enonce_markdown: Two angles of a triangle are $47^\circ$ and $68^\circ$. (a) Find the third angle. (b) One side is extended at the vertex of the $68^\circ$ angle. Find the exterior angle formed there.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) $180^\circ-47^\circ-68^\circ=65^\circ$.

**Answer: $65^\circ$.**

(b) The exterior angle lies on a straight line with the $68^\circ$ angle, so it is $180^\circ-68^\circ=112^\circ$. Check with the exterior angle rule: $47^\circ+65^\circ=112^\circ$.

**Answer: $112^\circ$.**

items.enonce_markdown: A regular polygon has 18 sides. Find (a) each exterior angle, (b) each interior angle, (c) the sum of the interior angles.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) $\dfrac{360^\circ}{18}=20^\circ$. **Each exterior angle is $20^\circ$.**

(b) $180^\circ-20^\circ=160^\circ$. **Each interior angle is $160^\circ$.**

(c) $(18-2)\times 180^\circ=16\times 180^\circ=2880^\circ$. Check: $18\times 160^\circ=2880^\circ$.

**Answer: $2880^\circ$.**

items.enonce_markdown: The interior angles of a pentagon are $x^\circ$, $(x+20)^\circ$, $2x^\circ$, $(2x-10)^\circ$ and $110^\circ$. Find $x$ and the size of the largest angle.
items.solution_markdown:
The interior angles of a pentagon add up to $(5-2)\times 180^\circ=540^\circ$.

$x+(x+20)+2x+(2x-10)+110=540$

$6x+120=540$, so $6x=420$ and $x=70$.

The angles are $70^\circ$, $90^\circ$, $140^\circ$, $130^\circ$ and $110^\circ$; their sum is $540^\circ$, as required.

**Answer: $x=70$ and the largest angle is $140^\circ$.**

items_markdown: Angles on a straight line add to $180^\circ$; angles around a point add to $360^\circ$; vertically opposite angles are equal.
Parallel lines: corresponding and alternate angles are equal, co-interior angles add to $180^\circ$.
The interior angles of an $n$-sided polygon add to $(n-2)\times 180^\circ$.
Exterior angles of any polygon add to $360^\circ$; for a regular polygon each one is $\dfrac{360^\circ}{n}$.
Interior angle plus exterior angle at a vertex is $180^\circ$. Give a reason for every angle you write down.
